references.text: Psalm 68:2 contains a similar prayer for God to arise and His enemies to be scattered, reflecting the words from Numbers 10:35-36 regarding the movement of the ark.
Psalm 132:8 contains a prayer for the Lord to return to His resting place along with the ark of the covenant, corresponding to the prayer for the Lord to return to Israel's ten thousands.
Psalm 90:13 uses the verb 'return' (שׁוּבָה) in a prayer to the Lord, using the same wording as in Numbers 10:36.
The blessing over Rebekah mentions 'thousands of ten thousands,' the same expression for Israel's great multitude found in Numbers 10:36.
In Moses' blessing, the Lord is described as coming from Sinai with ten thousands of holy ones, reflecting the concept of the Lord in the midst of Israel's ten thousands.
